## `meshforge/v1/agent.proto`

> **Status:** current. The agent <-> controller session (ADR-0002).

Controller <-> agent control plane (ARCHITECTURE §20, ADR-0002).

Each agent dials OUT to the controller and holds one long-lived bidirectional
stream. Agent -> controller: AgentMessage; controller -> agent:
ControllerMessage. Both are envelopes with a `payload` oneof.

Delivery semantics (ARCHITECTURE §13): at-least-once, exactly-once effect.
Every envelope carries a unique `message_id`; for ControllerMessage it is the
command ID the agent deduplicates on. Receipts flow both ways with the same
Ack message (ADR-0002): the controller acks agent reports so the agent can
drop them from its reconnect buffer, and the agent acks controller commands
so the controller stops re-sending them.

Fencing: every payload that refers to an attempt (has `attempt_id`) also
carries that attempt's `fencing_token` (enforced by tests/unit/test_protos.py).

Session fencing (ADR-0002 Updates 2026-09-20, roadmap 0.3.1):
- The agent persists a `session_epoch` counter with its identity (ADR-0013),
  increments it before every new stream and sends it in Hello. The controller
  keeps at most one live session per node_id: a Hello with a HIGHER epoch than
  the live session's closes that older stream (a zombie); a LOWER or EQUAL
  epoch is rejected with HelloAck{accepted=false, reject_code=STALE_EPOCH}.
  Epochs are never compared across node_ids.
- The controller answers Hello with HelloAck{session_id, heartbeat_interval_ms,
  lease_ms}. Both sides put that session_id in envelope field 3 of every
  later message; a message carrying another session's id is dropped and
  counted, never processed. Intervals are controller-owned.
- After a reconnect the agent sends Reconcile{replay_from_sequence} and
  replays its bounded ring of un-acked reports; the controller dedupes on
  message_id. Heartbeats are never buffered or replayed.
- Liveness (ARCHITECTURE §12.3) is measured on the controller's monotonic
  clock; the Timestamps in Heartbeat/HelloAck are for RTT and display only.

Roadmap coverage: 0.1.5 envelopes/oneofs; 0.3.1 session/liveness/resource
payloads; 0.3.4 hardware scores; 0.4.6 attempt execution (ExecutionSpec,
AttemptStatus results). TODO(V0.4 G5): LogChunk flow. V0.5: CacheReport (D101), peer endpoint/key (D98/D99), G5: GcRequest, PrepareEnv/PrepareEnvStatus, InputTree, TransferSummary. TODO(V0.6): network probes for scheduling.

Package `meshforge.v1`.

### service `AgentControl`

| RPC | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Session` | `stream AgentMessage` | `stream ControllerMessage` | One stream per connected agent. Opened by the agent. |
| `RenewCertificate` | `RenewCertificateRequest` | `RenewCertificateResponse` | V0.7 G4 (roadmap 0.7.7b, D140): a new node certificate for the caller, identified ONLY by the mutual-TLS client certificate of this call. The CSR must name that node in this fabric and be signed by its key (a new key = `meshforge-agent rotate-key`). The new certificate is "pending" until the node's first Hello with it; only then is the old serial superseded, so a renewal never cuts the live session. Refusals: gRPC status + trailing `meshforge-reason` (csr_<pki reason>, renew_node_mismatch, node_revoked, cert_superseded, rate_limited, unavailable, internal). |

| `peer_endpoint` | 10 | `string` | - | "host:port" the agent's peer blob server listens on (V0.5 D97/D99); empty = no peer server. | `max_cpu_jobs` | 11 | `uint32` | optional | Slots (V0.6 D105): how many jobs of each kind the owner lets this node run at once ([agent.execution] max_cpu_jobs / max_gpu_jobs). Absent = not said (an older agent): the controller assumes 1 CPU slot, and 1 GPU slot only with the exec-gpu capability. 0 = no jobs of that kind. The controller ignores a value above 64 (logged) and caps the total per node with its own [controller.jobs] max_attempts_per_node. |
| `max_gpu_jobs` | 12 | `uint32` | optional | - |
| `policy` | 13 | `OwnerPolicy` | - | The owner's policy (V0.7 G5, D142). Absent = an agent from before G5: the controller assumes an open policy (its agent enforces what it enforces). A present but malformed or oversized policy is refused as a whole: the node is treated as accepting nothing (fail closed), never trusted partially. |
| `display_name` | 14 | `string` | - | V0.7 G3: node identity is proven by the client certificate (mTLS); node_id must equal the certificate's. V0.17 G3 (Q27): the friendly name the laptop's owner gave it in the local console (or [agent] node_name); empty = none, the dashboard shows the hostname. Printable, at most 64 characters: the controller refuses the Hello (INVALID_ARGUMENT) for a control character and clips nothing. |

#### message `OwnerPolicy`

The node owner's policy (V0.7 G5, roadmap 0.7.8, D142). The agent is
authoritative: it re-checks every StartAttempt against its current policy;
the controller's planner uses this copy to avoid sending what would be
refused. See common/owner_policy.py for the rule both sides apply.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accept_jobs` | 1 | `bool` | - | - |
| `accept_gpu_sessions` | 2 | `bool` | - | Stored and advertised now; Remote-GPU sessions use it from V0.11. |
| `max_ram_bytes` | 3 | `uint64` | optional | Per-job limits; absent = no owner limit. |
| `max_cpu_percent` | 4 | `uint32` | optional | 1..100: share of the node's CPU threads one job may use. |
| `max_vram_bytes` | 5 | `uint64` | optional | - |
| `allow_unsandboxed` | 6 | `bool` | - | - |
| `allow_network` | 7 | `bool` | - | A job asking `limits.network: on` may get a network (D143). |
| `allowed_users` | 8 | `string` | repeated | User names whose jobs the node runs; empty = everyone (<= 64 names). |
| `not_enforced` | 9 | `string` | repeated | "<field>:<why>" caps this OS/runtime cannot enforce with a runtime limit (e.g. "max_vram_bytes:no_runtime_limit"); <= 16 entries. |
| `revision` | 10 | `uint64` | - | Agent-local counter, +1 per live change (logs only). |
| `pause_benchmarks` | 11 | `bool` | - | V0.9 G5 (D219/D246): the owner paused benchmark jobs on this node (`meshforge-agent bench pause`). User jobs are not affected. Default false, so an agent from before G5 keeps running benchmarks. |

An agent's announced, orderly end of its stream (V0.4 D40). See the payload

#### message `CacheReport`

What a node holds in its caches (V0.5 D90/D100/D101). A report: buffered,
replayed after a reconnect and acked like ResourceUpdate. After every
accepted Hello the agent sends a paged SNAPSHOT (snapshot=true on every page,
snapshot_last=true on the final one), then deltas (snapshot=false). The
controller replaces the node's rows on the first snapshot page of a new
session and applies deltas only after snapshot_last. A delta that arrives
before it is dropped; one with a gap in `seq` marks the node's index stale
until the agent's next snapshot (every Hello and periodically). At most 1024
items in added + removed together; keys are validated by kind.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `seq` | 1 | `uint64` | - | Monotonic per agent PROCESS (never reset by a reconnect), > 0: a report replayed from an earlier session of the same process is recognisably old. |
| `snapshot` | 2 | `bool` | - | This message is a page of a full snapshot (added = what is held now). |
| `snapshot_last` | 3 | `bool` | - | The final page of the snapshot; deltas follow. |
| `added` | 4 | `CacheItem` | repeated | - |
| `removed` | 5 | `CacheItem` | repeated | Always empty on a snapshot page. |
| `page` | 6 | `uint32` | optional | V0.5 G4 fix round 2 (additive): index of this page within its snapshot, 0 = the first page; 0 on a delta. Only page 0 starts (replaces) a snapshot, so a session whose first report is the TAIL of a snapshot (its head acked on an earlier session) never goes live with partial rows - the D101 fields alone cannot tell a first page from a tail after a loss. `optional` (fix round 3): an agent that predates the field sends none, and "absent" must not read as "page 0" - the controller then accepts only a single-page snapshot; a multi-page one makes the node stale (logged). |

#### message `NetProbeResult`

The answer to a ProbeRequest (V0.6 G4, D111): what this node measured
downloading from the target's peer server. A report: buffered, replayed after
a reconnect and acked. ok = false -> `error` names why (a stable code) and the
numbers are 0; `bytes` is still what was transferred (the probe budget).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `probe_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `target_node_id` | 2 | `string` | - | - |
| `ok` | 3 | `bool` | - | - |
| `rtt_ms` | 4 | `double` | - | Median of the 0-byte request round trips (ms). |
| `bw_bytes_s` | 5 | `double` | - | Throughput of the largest timed download (bytes/s). |
| `bytes` | 6 | `uint64` | - | Every body byte received during the probe. |
| `duration_s` | 7 | `double` | - | Wall time of the whole probe (s). |
| `error` | 8 | `string` | - | - |

#### message `AttemptStatus`

One attempt state change, reported by the agent through send_report (buffered,
replayed after a reconnect, acked). The controller applies it idempotently on
(attempt_id, fencing_token, state) and drops a report whose fencing_token is not
the attempt's current one (counted as `fenced`). V0.4 D52/D67/D68.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `attempt_id` | 2 | `string` | - | - |
| `fencing_token` | 3 | `uint64` | - | Monotonic attempt epoch; the controller rejects reports with a stale token. |
| `state` | 4 | `AttemptState` | - | - |
| `failure` | 5 | `Failure` | - | Set only when state == ATTEMPT_STATE_FAILED. |
| `observed_at` | 6 | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | - | - |
| `exit_code` | 7 | `int32` | optional | The workload's exit code, once it exited (absent: it never ran, or its status could not be read). On an env_error "setup_failed" it is the setup step's. |
| `phases` | 8 | `PhaseTimings` | - | Agent-measured phase durations (monotonic clock). Sent in the terminal status; an absent field means the phase never ran (the controller records it skipped). |
| `output_digest` | 9 | `string` | - | "sha256:<64 hex>" of the packed outputs (V0.4 G5); empty until then. |
| `missing_outputs` | 10 | `string` | repeated | Declared outputs (manifest `outputs`) that matched nothing (bounded). Not an error: listed so the user sees it (D54). |
| `runtime` | 11 | `string` | - | Runtime that ran (or was chosen to run) the attempt: "docker" \| "venv" \| "subprocess". |
| `signal` | 12 | `int32` | optional | Signal number that ended the workload, when it died by one. |
| `stdout_log` | 13 | `FinalLog` | - | The attempt's complete local logs, uploaded with its upload grant in the terminal status (V0.4 G5, D71). Absent: not uploaded (stopped attempt, empty log, upload failed) - the controller keeps its live copy then. |
| `stderr_log` | 14 | `FinalLog` | - | - |
| `transfers` | 15 | `TransferSummary` | repeated | Transfer telemetry (V0.5 G5, D93): one entry per staged tree (the project tree first, then named inputs), sent with the terminal status. At most 1 + 16 entries; the controller persists them as transfer_event rows. |
| `env_hash` | 16 | `string` | - | The environment the runtime resolved or tried to build (V0.6 G1, D116): 64 lowercase hex of the agent's env hash, empty when none was computed. Terminal statuses only. An env_error with a hash makes the controller remember (node, env) as known-bad for [controller.jobs] env_bad_ttl_s. |
| `workload` | 17 | `WorkloadReport` | - | V0.9 G1 (D212): a benchmark's own report (results/workload.json); absent for any other job. Terminal statuses only. |
| `condition` | 18 | `ConditionReport` | - | V0.9 G4 (D217): what the agent did with StartAttempt.condition (terminal statuses only; absent when the attempt had none). |

#### message `ConditionReport`

The outcome of a benchmark condition on the agent (V0.9 G4).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | 1 | `string` | - | The canonical condition string it applied (echoes BenchCondition.spec). |
| `verified` | 2 | `bool` | - | Applied and verified (measured values within the condition's bound). |
| `measured_json` | 3 | `string` | - | What was measured, a JSON object (<= 2048 characters), e.g. {"cores":2,"load_cores":1.97,"window_s":2.0}. "" = nothing measured. |
| `reason` | 4 | `string` | - | Why it could not be applied or verified; "" when verified. |
| `reverted` | 5 | `bool` | - | The condition was reverted cleanly at the attempt's end (false: the revert failed and the marker keeps it for the next start's sweep). |

#### message `TransferSummary`

What staging one tree cost (V0.5 G5, D93). Agent-measured, monotonic clock.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_id` | 1 | `string` | - | "sha256:<64 hex>" of the staged tree. |
| `blobs_hit` | 2 | `uint32` | - | Blobs (and their bytes) that were already in the agent's cache: hits. |
| `bytes_hit` | 3 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `blobs_fetched` | 4 | `uint32` | - | Blobs fetched now (misses) and the payload bytes received for them. |
| `bytes_fetched` | 5 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `chunks_resumed` | 6 | `uint32` | - | Chunks a previous interrupted fetch had already verified (not re-sent). |
| `corrupt_refetches` | 7 | `uint32` | - | Whole blobs fetched again after a corrupt copy was found. |
| `manifest_hit` | 8 | `bool` | - | The tree manifest came from the cache. |
| `duration_s` | 9 | `double` | - | Fetch + verify + copy into the workdir. |
| `sources` | 10 | `TransferSource` | repeated | Per source (at most 17: the controller + 16 peers). |

#### message `TransferSource`

One blob source's share of a tree's transfer (V0.5 D89/D93).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `bytes` | 2 | `uint64` | - | Payload bytes received from it (wasted end-game duplicates included). |
| `duration_s` | 3 | `double` | - | Time spent in requests to it (overlapping requests add up). |
| `units` | 4 | `uint32` | - | Units (chunks or whole blobs) it won. |
| `failures` | 5 | `uint32` | - | - |
| `dropped` | 6 | `string` | - | Why it was dropped for this transfer (a failure_type value); empty = kept. |

#### message `FinalLog`

One stream's final log (D71).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `digest` | 1 | `string` | - | "sha256:<64 hex>" of the uploaded log blob; empty = not uploaded. |
| `bytes` | 2 | `uint64` | - | Bytes of workload output kept (the cap stops the file growing). |
| `truncated` | 3 | `bool` | - | The workload wrote more than the per-stream cap; the rest was dropped and a marker line says so at the end of the log. |

#### message `PhaseTimings`

Durations in seconds on the agent's monotonic clock (ARCHITECTURE §17, D68).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stage_s` | 1 | `double` | optional | Bundle fetch + digest check + unpack. |
| `env_s` | 2 | `double` | optional | Image pull + requirements install (the runtime's env phase). |
| `run_s` | 3 | `double` | optional | Workload start to exit. |
| `collect_s` | 4 | `double` | optional | Workload exit to the terminal report (output packing/upload from G5 on). |
| `compute_ns` | 5 | `uint64` | optional | V0.9 G1 (D213): the workload's own kernel time in nanoseconds, measured by the workload with a monotonic clock and read by the agent from its results/workload.json (benchmark jobs). Absent for every other job. |

#### message `WorkloadReport`

V0.9 G1 (D212): what a benchmark job said about itself in
results/workload.json, read once by the agent after the workload exited
(bounded, untrusted: the workload wrote it). Terminal statuses only.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `family` | 1 | `string` | - | Family name, e.g. "cpu.matmul" (<= 64 chars, [a-z0-9_.-]); "" = unreadable. |
| `params_json` | 2 | `string` | - | The parameters as canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact; <= 4096 chars); "" = absent or too large. |
| `seed` | 3 | `uint64` | optional | - |
| `status` | 4 | `string` | - | "ok" \| "check_failed" \| "unavailable" \| "bad_params". |
| `device` | 5 | `string` | - | "cpu" \| "cuda" \| "" (not run). |
| `result_schema_version` | 6 | `uint32` | - | results/workload.json schema_version (0 = absent). |
| `compute_iterations` | 7 | `uint32` | optional | How many iterations compute_ns covers (D225/D228: compute_ns is the whole timed loop; one iteration = compute_ns / compute_iterations). Unset = not run or not reported. 1..100000 (the largest loop parameter of a family). |

#### message `LogChunk`

Live log bytes (D71): best-effort, never buffered or replayed, never acked.
`offset` is the byte position of `data` in the attempt's stream on the agent;
a chunk dropped on the way shows up as a jump (a gap the controller records).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `attempt_id` | 2 | `string` | - | - |
| `stream` | 3 | `LogChunk.Stream` | - | - |
| `offset` | 4 | `uint64` | - | Byte offset of `data` within the stream, for dedupe after reconnect. |
| `data` | 5 | `bytes` | - | - |
| `fencing_token` | 6 | `uint64` | - | Attempt epoch; logs from a fenced (superseded) attempt are dropped. |

#### enum `LogChunk.Stream`

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `STREAM_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | - |
| `STREAM_STDOUT` | 1 | - |
| `STREAM_STDERR` | 2 | - |

#### message `StartAttempt`

Run one attempt (V0.4 D52/D67). The agent dedupes on (attempt_id,
fencing_token), not only on message_id: the controller resends the SAME
attempt after a reconnect or its own restart (D66), with a new message_id.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `attempt_id` | 2 | `string` | - | - |
| `fencing_token` | 3 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `spec` | 4 | `ExecutionSpec` | - | - |
| `secrets` | 5 | `JobSecret` | repeated | V0.7 G6 (D144): the values of the job owner's secrets the manifest names (ExecutionSpec.manifest_json "secrets"), one entry per name. Sent only on a mutually authenticated (mTLS) session - never in insecure-dev unless [security] allow_insecure_secrets. The agent holds them in memory and in the attempt's private secret files only; never logged, never persisted, wiped when the attempt ends. |
| `condition` | 6 | `BenchCondition` | - | V0.9 G4 (D217/D241): the benchmark condition of this attempt; absent for every other job (and for conditions the controller applies itself, e.g. queue). The agent applies it BEFORE staging, verifies it (an unverified condition fails the attempt config_error "condition_failed:..." - nothing runs, the run is never labelled), and reverts it when the attempt ends, on every path (done, failure, cancel, agent stop; a persisted marker is swept at the next agent start after a crash). The agent re-validates the string and refuses a kind it did not advertise. |
| `benchmark` | 7 | `bool` | - | V0.9 G5 (D219/D246): this attempt is a benchmark job (a campaign run, a queue filler or a cache warm-up). The agent refuses it - and stops it if it runs - while the owner paused benchmarks or is using the laptop (failure owner_preempted); it never stops a job without this flag. |
| `lane` | 8 | `LaneSpec` | - | V0.10 G4 (D259): present = this attempt is a LANE of a Mode 3 (split) job. The agent stages the project and builds the env once, then pulls chunks (ChunkRequest) and runs the entrypoint once per chunk. An agent that does not know this field never gets a lane: the controller places lanes only on nodes advertising the "exec-split" capability. |
| `combine` | 9 | `CombineSpec` | - | V0.10 G5 (D268/D283): present = this attempt is the COMBINE of a split job: it fetches every chunk's committed result (the parts index, chunk order), unpacks them read-only as parts/NNNNN in an agent-owned folder outside any workdir, runs the built-in (concat, merge-csv, merge-json: trusted agent code in its own process) or the user's combine script (sandboxed like any job, project staged), and reports the packed out/ folder as the attempt's (= the job's) output. Placed only on nodes that advertise "exec-split" (agents of this version run both lanes and combines). |

#### message `CombineSpec`

A split job's combine (V0.10 G5, D268).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parts_digest` | 1 | `string` | - | "sha256:<64 hex>" of the parts index blob (common/split_chunks.py: every chunk's result digest in chunk order). The attempt's fetch token may read it and every part it names; the agent verifies every digest. |
| `chunk_count` | 2 | `uint32` | - | Chunks in the index (the agent checks the index has exactly these). |

#### message `LaneSpec`

A lane's chunk source (V0.10 G4, D259/D263/D264).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items_digest` | 1 | `string` | - | "sha256:<64 hex>" of the job's item list (the canonical JSON blob of common/split_items.py, resolved once at submit). The attempt's fetch token may read it; the agent verifies its digest before use. |
| `item_count` | 2 | `uint32` | - | - |
| `max_chunk_output_bytes` | 3 | `uint64` | - | Bytes one chunk's packed output may have (split.max_chunk_output_bytes); more fails the chunk output_error. |
| `lease_timeout_s` | 4 | `double` | - | The lease (visibility) timeout; the agent renews its live leases every third of it (LeaseRenew). |

#### message `BenchCondition`

One benchmark condition (V0.9 G4). ``spec`` is the canonical condition
string of common/bench_conditions.py ("cpu_load:2", "cache:cold",
"netem:delay=50ms,loss=1%"), <= 64 characters.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | 1 | `string` | - | - |

One secret value for one attempt (V0.7 G6). ``name`` follows

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `value` | 2 | `bytes` | - | - |

#### message `ExecutionSpec`

What to run and with what (V0.4 D52). Built by the controller from the job's
canonical manifest; every field is re-validated by the agent before use.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bundle_digest` | 1 | `string` | - | "sha256:<64 hex>" of the project bundle of a V0.4 bundle job. Empty for a tree job (V0.5 G4: a tree job is named only by tree_id). |
| `blob_url` | 2 | `string` | - | Base URL of the blob API ("http://host:port") when the controller has an advertised URL; empty = the agent uses http://<host it dialled>:<blob_port>. |
| `blob_port` | 3 | `uint32` | - | The controller's REST port, used when blob_url is empty. |
| `fetch_token` | 4 | `string` | - | Per-attempt fetch token (D48): may read exactly this attempt's digests - download-only (D73). A secret: never logged, never persisted. |
| `manifest_json` | 5 | `string` | - | The canonical manifest JSON (common.manifest.Manifest.canonical_json()). |
| `runtime` | 6 | `string` | - | Runtime the controller asks for ("docker" \| "venv" \| "subprocess"); empty = the agent chooses among what it offers (sandboxed first, D51). V0.4 sends empty. |
| `memory_bytes` | 7 | `uint64` | - | 0 = the agent's default for that limit. |
| `cpus` | 8 | `double` | - | - |
| `gpu_indices` | 9 | `uint32` | repeated | NVML indices of the GPUs this attempt may use (HardwareSummary.Gpu.index); empty = no GPU. |
| `timeout_s` | 10 | `uint32` | - | The workload's own time limit in seconds (manifest limits.timeout). |
| `output_globs` | 11 | `string` | repeated | Declared outputs (manifest `outputs`), collected in V0.4 G5. |
| `upload_token` | 12 | `string` | - | Upload grant (V0.4 G5, D73): the only credential that may PUT blobs for this attempt (outputs archive + final logs), within the two quotas below and only while the attempt is live. A secret: never logged, never persisted. |
| `upload_max_bytes` | 13 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `upload_max_blobs` | 14 | `uint32` | - | - |
| `tree_id` | 15 | `string` | - | V0.5 D83: "sha256:<64 hex>" of the project's tree manifest (D81); empty = a V0.4 bundle job. The agent fetches the manifest and the blobs it names into its CAS, verifying every chunk and blob, then copies them into the workdir. |
| `sources` | 16 | `BlobSource` | repeated | Where the blobs may be fetched (V0.5 D83/D89/D100): the controller first, then up to [controller.jobs] max_peer_sources ONLINE peers holding the tree, each with its own signed peer token (D98). The agent fetches from all of them in parallel, work-stealing. |
| `inputs` | 17 | `InputTree` | repeated | Named inputs (V0.5 G5, D92), at most 16: each tree is fetched like the project tree and copied READ-ONLY to its mount path inside the workdir. |
| `owner_name` | 18 | `string` | - | V0.7 G5 (D142): the job owner's user name as the controller knows it (empty = unknown, e.g. a legacy fabric-token job). The agent checks it against [agent.policy] allowed_users; an empty name never matches a list. |

#### message `InputTree`

One named input of an attempt (V0.5 D92).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_id` | 1 | `string` | - | "sha256:<64 hex>" of the input's tree manifest. |
| `mount` | 2 | `string` | - | Relative POSIX path inside the workdir (validated by both sides: no "..", not absolute, not overlapping the project or another input). |
| `ref` | 3 | `string` | - | What the manifest named ("name@version" or "name@sha256:..."), for logs. |
| `sources` | 4 | `BlobSource` | repeated | Where the input's blobs may be fetched: the controller first (the attempt's fetch token, which also covers every input tree) then peers holding THIS tree, each with a peer token scoped to it. |

One place an agent may download blobs from (V0.5 D83).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |

| `token` | 2 | `string` | - | Bearer token for that source (the attempt's fetch token for the controller). A secret: never logged, never persisted. |
| `node_id` | 3 | `string` | - | The holder's node_id; empty = the controller. |

#### message `CancelAttempt`

Stop an attempt (D69). `release` (V0.4 G5, D75): the controller has already
ended this attempt (or never knew it) - stop it if it still runs, then forget
it and free its workdir at once, without waiting for an Ack of its terminal
report (nothing the agent reports about it will be applied).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `fencing_token` | 2 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `reason` | 3 | `string` | - | - |
| `release` | 4 | `bool` | - | - |

#### message `RefreshFetchToken`

Replaces the fetch token of a held attempt (V0.5, D95). Same scope as the
token in its StartAttempt (download-only, the attempt's bundle or tree); the
old token is not revived. The agent applies it only to the attempt with this
(attempt_id, fencing_token) and only while it still stages; a staging that
was refused (401) or could not reach the controller retries with it.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `fencing_token` | 2 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `fetch_token` | 3 | `string` | - | A secret: never logged, never persisted. |
| `blob_url` | 4 | `string` | - | Where the restarted controller serves blobs now (like ExecutionSpec fields 2/3): a restart may come up on another port or advertised URL. Replaces the StartAttempt's values for this attempt's controller fetches. |
| `blob_port` | 5 | `uint32` | - | - |
| `sources` | 6 | `BlobSource` | repeated | The attempt's source list re-minted (V0.5 D98): the controller first (its token = fetch_token above) then peer holders with fresh peer tokens. Replaces the StartAttempt's ExecutionSpec.sources for this attempt. |
| `inputs` | 7 | `InputTree` | repeated | The attempt's named inputs with their sources re-minted (V0.5 G5). |

#### message `RefreshPeerTokens`

Peer tokens re-minted for a staging attempt (V0.7 G3, D147). Each token
replaces the one the attempt holds for the same (tree_id, node_id) - the
StartAttempt's or an earlier refresh's; a pair the attempt was never given
is ignored (the list of peers is the StartAttempt's / RefreshFetchToken's).
Applied only to the attempt with this (attempt_id, fencing_token) while it
has not ended. Not re-sent on a missing Ack: the next re-mint supersedes it.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `fencing_token` | 2 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `tokens` | 3 | `PeerTokenGrant` | repeated | - |

#### message `RevocationUpdate`

Node certificate serials no plane of the fabric accepts any more (V0.7 G3,
D138): revoked nodes and certificates superseded by a re-enrolment, whose
certificates have not expired yet. Lower-case hex, no "0x", at most 40
chars each; the newest first, at most 10000. Serials are only ever added
(there is no un-revoke): the agent keeps the union of every set it got.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `serials` | 1 | `string` | repeated | - |

#### message `PeerTokenGrant`

One re-minted peer token: `node_id` may be asked for the blobs of `tree_id`
with `token` (D98 scope: this tree, this requester, this holder, this
attempt; <= 60 s). A secret: never logged, never persisted.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tree_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `node_id` | 2 | `string` | - | - |
| `token` | 3 | `string` | - | - |

#### message `RefreshUploadGrant`

Replaces the upload grant of a held attempt (V0.6 G1, D114). Same quota as
the grant in its StartAttempt (what earlier grants of the attempt already
stored is NOT known to a restarted controller). Applied only to the attempt
with this (attempt_id, fencing_token) while it has not ended; an upload that
was refused (401) or could not reach the controller retries with it,
resuming the parts the controller already holds.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `fencing_token` | 2 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `upload_token` | 3 | `string` | - | A secret: never logged, never persisted. |
| `blob_url` | 4 | `string` | - | Where the controller serves blobs now (like ExecutionSpec fields 2/3). |
| `blob_port` | 5 | `uint32` | - | - |

#### message `ProbeRequest`

"ProbeLink" (V0.6 G4, D111): measure the link from `target_node_id`'s peer
server to this node. The agent sends `rtt_samples` 0-byte GETs to
http://<endpoint>/v1/probe?bytes=0 (median = RTT), then one GET of `bytes`
zero bytes, and one of `max_bytes` if that took less than `fast_s`; it answers
with NetProbeResult{same probe_id}. `token` is a controller-signed probe
token (kind "probe", holder = target, requester = this node, <= 60 s).
Idempotent by probe_id: a repeated probe_id is never measured twice.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `probe_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `target_node_id` | 2 | `string` | - | - |
| `endpoint` | 3 | `string` | - | host:port of the target's peer server (its Hello.peer_endpoint). |
| `token` | 4 | `string` | - | - |
| `rtt_samples` | 5 | `uint32` | - | - |
| `bytes` | 6 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `max_bytes` | 7 | `uint64` | - | - |
| `fast_s` | 8 | `double` | - | - |

Pull base images / build environments ahead of a run (V0.5 G5, roadmap
0.5.8 `compute node prepare`). Idempotent: an image already present or an
env already built is reported `hit`; the same request_id twice runs once.
The agent answers with PrepareEnvStatus reports.

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env_hash` | 1 | `string` | - | V0.1 placeholder, never sent and ignored (kept: V0.1 numbers are pinned). |
| `request_id` | 2 | `string` | - | ULID chosen by the controller; echoed in every PrepareEnvStatus. |
| `base_images` | 3 | `string` | repeated | Base image names ("python-cpu", "cuda-pytorch"), pinned by digest on the agent ([agent.execution.images]); at most 8. |
| `envs` | 4 | `EnvSpecRequest` | repeated | Environments to build, at most 32. |

#### message `HelloAck`

Reply to Hello (ADR-0002 Updates §1-2). The controller's first message on
every stream. If `accepted` is false the controller closes the stream after
sending it; `reject_code` says why and the agent decides whether to retry
(STALE_EPOCH: bump epoch and reconnect; PROTOCOL_VERSION: never retry;
UNAVAILABLE / INTERNAL: back off and retry).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accepted` | 1 | `bool` | - | - |
| `session_id` | 2 | `string` | - | Set when accepted; both sides put it in envelope field 3 from now on. |
| `heartbeat_interval_ms` | 3 | `uint32` | - | Controller-owned liveness parameters (ARCHITECTURE §12.3, ADR-0002 §5). |
| `lease_ms` | 4 | `uint32` | - | - |
| `controller_time` | 5 | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | - | Controller wall clock when the ack was sent (clock-skew estimate only). |
| `reject_code` | 6 | `HelloAck.RejectCode` | - | Set only when accepted == false. |
| `reject_reason` | 7 | `string` | - | Human-readable detail for logs; must never contain secrets. |
| `peer_token_key` | 8 | `bytes` | - | The controller's Ed25519 public key (raw 32 bytes) that signs peer blob tokens (V0.5 D98). Set when accepted; the agent's peer server verifies tokens with the key of its CURRENT session only. |
| `revoked_serials` | 9 | `string` | repeated | The fabric's revocation set when the session was accepted (V0.7 G3, D138; same rules as RevocationUpdate.serials): a reconnecting agent catches up before its peer server serves anyone. |

#### enum `HelloAck.RejectCode`

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `REJECT_CODE_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | - |
| `REJECT_CODE_STALE_EPOCH` | 1 | Hello.session_epoch <= the live session's epoch for this node_id. |
| `REJECT_CODE_PROTOCOL_VERSION` | 2 | Hello.protocol_version outside the controller's supported range, or (V0.17 G5, D393) Hello.agent_version outside the accepted window - same and previous minor of the controller: reject_reason then starts with "version_unsupported:" and names both versions and the fix. The code is reused on purpose: agents too old to know a new code are the ones refused, and every agent stops (never retries) on PROTOCOL_VERSION. |
| `REJECT_CODE_DUPLICATE_SESSION` | 3 | Another stream for this node_id won a concurrent Hello race. |
| `REJECT_CODE_INTERNAL` | 4 | - |
| `REJECT_CODE_UNAVAILABLE` | 5 | The controller could not finish the admission in time (its database is slow or unreachable, V0.4 D41). Retryable: back off and try again. |

Controller -> agent. The agent replies immediately with Pong{ping_id}.

#### message `Pong`

Agent -> controller. Echoes Ping.ping_id.

Clock offset (V0.9 G1, D213): a Ping/Pong is also one NTP-style exchange.
The controller notes its wall clock at the Ping, the Pong's envelope
`sent_at` is the agent's wall clock when it answered, and the controller's
receive time is the Ping's wall time plus the monotonic RTT - so the
controller estimates (agent clock - controller clock) +- RTT/2 from a recent
window of exchanges. Older agents send no resolution (0 = unknown; the
controller then assumes a coarse tick and widens the bound).

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ping_id` | 1 | `string` | - | - |
| `clock_resolution_us` | 2 | `uint32` | - | Resolution of the agent's wall clock (the one that stamps `sent_at`), in microseconds, from time.get_clock_info("time"); 0 = not reported. Windows on Python 3.12 ticks in ~15.6 ms steps, so the bound must cover it. |

## `meshforge/v1/common.proto`

> **Status:** current. Shared types.

MeshForge shared contract types (ARCHITECTURE §12, §13, §20).

SKELETON (roadmap task 0.1.5): only the essential shared types exist here.
Later versions flesh them out: TODO(V0.3) session/liveness types,
TODO(V0.4) attempt execution details, TODO(V0.11) GPU-plane types.

Conventions (protobuf style guide):
- IDs are strings (ULIDs from meshforge.common.ids).
- Times are google.protobuf.Timestamp; durations are google.protobuf.Duration.
- Every enum has a *_UNSPECIFIED = 0 value; receivers must treat it as "not set".
- Removed fields/values must be listed in `reserved`; never reuse a number.

Package `meshforge.v1`.

## `meshforge/v1/enroll.proto`

> **Status:** current. Join-code enrolment (ADR-0016).

Pairing a laptop with the fabric (V0.7 G2, D136/D150, ADR-0016).

G2 serves this service on an interim TLS listener of its own
([controller.enroll] bind, default port 47101): the controller presents its
server certificate (issued by the fabric CA) together with the CA certificate
and asks for no client certificate. G3 folds it into the session port, where
Enroll stays the only RPC allowed without a client certificate.

The agent never sends the join token before it has pinned the CA:
  1. it reads the CA certificate from the TLS handshake (verification off),
     and compares the first 128 bits of SHA-256(CA DER) with the code's pin;
  2. only then it opens a VERIFYING channel (root = that CA, target name
     "meshforge-controller") and calls Enroll.

A refusal is a gRPC status with trailing metadata `meshforge-reason` (a stable
code such as token_used, csr_bad_signature, node_key_conflict); messages
never echo the token or the CSR.

Package `meshforge.v1`.

### service `Enrollment`

| RPC | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Enroll` | `EnrollRequest` | `EnrollResponse` | Redeem a single-use join token for a node certificate. Unauthenticated by design (the token is the credential); rate-limited per source IP. |

### Messages

#### message `EnrollRequest`

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `join_token` | 1 | `bytes` | - | The 16 token bytes of the join code (D135). Never logged. |
| `csr_pem` | 2 | `bytes` | - | PEM CertificateSigningRequest signed by the node's ADR-0013 P-256 key, with exactly one SAN URI meshforge://fabric/<fabric_id>/node/<node_id>. At most 4096 bytes. |

#### message `EnrollResponse`

| Field | Number | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node_cert_pem` | 1 | `bytes` | - | The node certificate (30 days, EKU clientAuth + serverAuth), PEM. |
| `ca_cert_pem` | 2 | `bytes` | - | The fabric CA certificate, PEM (the same one the agent pinned). |
| `fabric_id` | 3 | `string` | - | - |
| `node_id` | 4 | `string` | - | The node_id the certificate names (echo of the CSR's, for the agent's check). |

## `meshforge/v1/gpu.proto`

> **Status:** deferred. Mode 2 / Mode 4 skeleton (ADR-0005), not built in v1.0 (ADR-0012): no process serves GpuService in this release.

GPU plane: GpuService, hosted by the GPU-service process on NVIDIA-GPU
laptops (ARCHITECTURE §3, §10, §11, §20; ADR-0005).

Remoting is at the PyTorch level: sessions own remote tensor handles and
modules shipped as torch.export ExportedPrograms (never pickled code).
Tensors travel as raw bytes + dtype/shape in chunked streams.

Errors: RPCs fail with a gRPC status; a typed meshforge.v1.Failure is
attached as status details. TODO(V0.11): define the rich-error mapping.

Chunking: TensorChunk.data is at most 1 MiB (MAX_TENSOR_CHUNK_BYTES in the
client/server code), well below gRPC's 4 MiB default max message size, so no
channel option changes are needed and envelope overhead fits comfortably.

TODO(V0.11): authenticate every session RPC (bind session_id to the
controller-issued session_token / node identity, not just OpenSession) and
add a per-request request_id for idempotent retries.

SKELETON (roadmap task 0.1.5). TODO(V0.11): Mode 2 fields in full.
TODO(V0.13): TrainStep and AllReduce* for Mode 4 training.

Package `meshforge.v1`.

### service `GpuService`

| RPC | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OpenSession` | `OpenSessionRequest` | `OpenSessionResponse` | - |
| `PutTensor` | `stream TensorChunk` | `PutTensorResponse` | Upload one tensor as a stream of chunks; the first chunk carries metadata. |
| `LoadModule` | `LoadModuleRequest` | `LoadModuleResponse` | - |
| `Call` | `CallRequest` | `CallResponse` | - |
| `GetTensor` | `GetTensorRequest` | `stream TensorChunk` | Download one tensor as a stream of chunks; the first chunk carries metadata. |
| `Free` | `FreeRequest` | `FreeResponse` | - |
| `TrainStep` | `TrainStepRequest` | `TrainStepResponse` | - |
| `CloseSession` | `CloseSessionRequest` | `CloseSessionResponse` | TODO(V0.13): AllReduce* collectives (coordinator-reduce, then ring). Their shape depends on the V0.2 cross-OS collectives spike, so they are not declared yet. |

### Messages

#### message `TensorMeta`

Payload layout: the tensor bytes are the tensor's storage made *contiguous,
row-major (C order)*, little-endian, with no strides/offset. Senders call
.contiguous() first; size_bytes == prod(shape) * element_size(dtype).
TODO(V0.11): revisit if non-contiguous views or big-endian hosts matter.
